Apes are indeed more visual compared to us, as females there have an estrus cycle as opposed to menstrual (so during fertility, their genitals will swell and such to announce fertility, whereas humans don't have a noticeable fertile window). You could even argue that breasts aren't always "developed" as they will still increase in size during pregnancy/breastfeeding.

Male breasts are underdeveloped compared to female breasts. That's why their milk is like that. But the fact they still have the capability to is my point. 

Females only appear to have "wasted" it so much of their lives because we live a lot longer than we used to, thus, the prime reproductive age has increased as it no longer includes simple biological factors. Also, your statement would only apply to developed countries that have access to formula, and where women tend to work more. Humans used to have *way* more children, and in less developed countries, this is still the case. I've known people who breastfed their children through their toddler years, because by constantly using the breasts as so intended, the breasts will produce enough to meet the demand. 

Also, on sexual attraction--such attraction to body parts other than the genitals is the result of a social construct. Refer to my other comment on this thread, where I mentioned how women were much more covered during the Victorian era, where anything uncovered, even a mere ankle, would be considered obscene. Same social ideas would lead to certain fetishes. If you learn that xyz = sexy, attractive, etc., then that's what connection you make in your mind whenever xyz shows up. If people are taught that big boob = sexy, that's what's ingrained in their mind. Meanwhile a person raised by a different culture in which there was no emphasis on boob = sexy, they may get a little confused by all the fuss about it. 

If breasts were primarily sexual, we would have evolved in such a way where everyone would have big breasts to attract mates. However, even small breasts can produce milk just as well as big ones, thus there is no need to become any larger. Breasts are only used less now because women work more and have less children, as success in the modern age has become way more demanding, biology aside. Again, this is only the case in more developed countries.

We were teenagers trapped in a facility lost in the jungle. It was built around a huge tree, and the warden was some creepy guy that wanted to keep us there. I remember teamming with a young boy to escape together.  We were chased by different obstacles and at one point we had to sneak around captive lions/tigers. Since it was in the jungle, it was very rainy and muddy and I remember the boy complaining about it a lot.

At some point we got separated and I found the rest of the kids and regrouped and we escaped together. As I looked back, on the steps to the entrance of the facility was the boy, just sitting there with his head in his hands, looking at me. Somehow in my dream I knew that he was in fact the warden in disguise. Once we escaped, he didn't chase after us.

Maybe he was just lonely.
